newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt upped in size, $3.0 bln priced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt upped in size, $3.0 bln priced.

text.p: U.S. investment grade and junk bond investors asked for and received substantial boosts in the size of several big deals on Friday, reflecting a still unquenched thirst for yield, dealers said.
High-grade deals totaling $2.25 billion and high-yield deals totaling $750 million were formally priced.

New issues featured $1.0 billion in 10-year notes from Morgan Stanley Group Inc via a Morgan Stanley & Co and Dean Witter Reynolds syndicate. The deal, first bandied about as $500 million, was upped first to $750 and then to its final size before pricing at 57 basis points over the curve.
The deal was expected to be priced in the 57 basis point to 59 basis point range. The already tightly priced paper was seen bid at par plus 1/8 in mid-afternoon.

Ford Motor Credit Corp issued $1.25 billion in five-year global bonds at a 38 basis point spread through Goldman Sachs & Co and Salomon Brothers Inc. That deal was also priced at the tight side of price talk and was increased in size on Thursday from $1.0 billion.
Secondary investment grade trade was shelved amid the wave of fresh supply and traders said spreads elsewhere were left virtually unscathed to marginally weaker.

Turning to the high-yield sector, Adelphia Communications Corp increased its 10-year B3/single-B senior note deal by $150 million to $350 million, and priced the notes as 9-7/8s to yield 10 percent or 364.3 basis points over Treasuries.

In a twist from recent trends, however, the bonds were said to trade poorly when freed and were quoted down on the day. The issue closed at 98-3/4 bid, 99-1/8 offer compared with its initial price of 99.217, one trader said.
Despite Adelphia's highly leveraged balance nature, analysts said the price drop was more a reflection of a too-aggressive pricing than weakness in the credit.
"It's a company that has much cheaper debt trading and this came too aggressive," said an analyst at a big New York shop. "And remember it was upped in size, too."
The deal was sold through sole manager Smith Barney Inc.

Elsewhere, Diamond Cable Communications Plc issued $250 million 10-year B3/B-minus senior discount notes with a five-year zero coupon to yield 10-3/4 percent through its majority owner Goldman, Sachs.
The privately placed issue, increased in size by $75 million, closed up about 1-1/2 points to 61 bid, 61-1/2 offer.

Packard Bioscience Co also tapped the high-yield market on Friday with $150 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, upped from $100 million, via Merrill Lynch, BA Securities and CIBC Wood Gundy Securities.
The B3/B-minus notes were priced in the private placement market to yield 9-3/8 percent or 300 basis points over.
High-yield secondary prices were mostly flat after a flurry of early activity, traders said.
In company specific news, Revlon Worldwide Corp's senior secured discount notes due 1998 popped more than one point on Friday after the company said it plans to defease the issue.

The debt was quoted as high as 93-1/2 bid, 94 offer at mid-morning compared with a 92-1/4 bid at Thursday's close, one trader said. The debt's spread tightened from about 260 basis points over Treasuries to 100 basis points over.
Traders expected the debt to move into the 50 to 75 basis point range over the next year.
Revlon Worldwide said it will raise funds to defease the debt through a new issuance of zero coupon bonds and a capital infusion by MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings Inc.
The U.S. T-bond closed up 6/32 to yield 6.64 percent.
